body:
I did some research and testing myself, and I can confirm that @KoBeWi appears to be correct that Windows does not actually appear to enforce any formatting on File Version / Product Version. However, RCEdit, which is the tool we use to modify these details does enforce some formatting.

RCEdit appears to have the following format requirements
File version - `0.0.0.0` format, as KoBe stated
Product version - Unlike what KoBe states, I could not input _any string_; it appears to accept any string that _begins with a number_. Aside from the number requirement at the start, it appears to allow everything else, it even allows special characters as shown below.

![](https://i.gyazo.com/9a3a8156f017ad66f1a7cee15d3f5bdb.png)


I'm not aware why we use RCEdit specifically or if we could potentially create our own fork of it to remove these restrictions. My basic suggestion is to allow users as much freedom as we can, since the OS itself has no enforcement, it would be interesting for any developers who want to hide easter eggs inside these fields. This would simply involve allowing users to do anything they want within the confines of RCEdit constraints.

I'll make a PR with the following changes
- Fixing the File Version warning to be more specific
- Fixing the Product Version warning to be more specific
- Editing the file warning logic to match the new "any string starting with a number" req
